lines.japanese: １２月の雑踏の中。俺はスクランブル交差点の際に立っていた。
lines.english: In the December crush, I stood at the edge of the scramble crossing.

lines.japanese: 昼はまだそれほどの寒さじゃない。冬という季節に縛られて厚着したひとびとの額は、皆ほのかに汗ばんでいる。
lines.english: It was not especially cold by day yet. Still, everyone had dressed for the season rather than the weather, and a faint sheen of sweat stood on every brow.

lines.japanese: 何十何百という見知らぬ人間たちが、信号待ちという共通目的のもとにひしめき合っている。
lines.english: Dozens—hundreds—of strangers jostled together with one purpose in common: waiting for the light.

lines.japanese: 四方から聞こえてくる声。誰のものとも知れない声。二度と聞くことのない声。
lines.english: Voices came from every direction. Voices whose owners I would never know. Voices I would never hear again.

lines.japanese: 俺を包みこむ雑踏のざわめきは、ときおり誰かの意思が垣間見える温かなノイズだ。
lines.english: The murmur of the crowd wrapped around me: warm noise in which, now and then, I caught a glimpse of somebody's will.

lines.japanese: 柳木原という巨大な集合体の中、俺はいま、さざめく雑踏に溶けこんでいる。
lines.english: Here, inside the immense collective called Yanagihara, I was dissolving into the murmuring crowd.

lines.japanese: 一年前。薄紫色の夜空の下、同じように信号待ちしていたことを思いだす。
lines.english: I remembered standing at a light just like this one a year ago, beneath a pale violet night sky.

lines.japanese: あれから色々なことがあった──
lines.english: A lot had happened since then—

lines.japanese: ──とは言っても、感傷に浸るほど年を食った覚えもない。
lines.english: —though I couldn't remember getting old enough to wallow in nostalgia.

lines.japanese: あのころと変わらない関係もあれば、変わっていった関係もある。
lines.english: Some relationships were the same as ever. Others had changed.

lines.japanese: 何人かは通行人Ａじゃなくなり、お互いの位置を確認しあう仲になった。
lines.english: Some people had stopped being Passerby A. We had come to know where we stood with each other.

lines.japanese: だからなんだって話。
lines.english: So what?

lines.japanese: 信号が青になり、四方向から一斉にひとがあふれ出た。天突きで押しだされるように俺も歩きだす。こんなところで突っぱっても意味がないんだ。
lines.english: The light turned green, and people flooded forward from all four directions at once. I started walking too, squeezed out with the crowd like jelly through a press. There was no point standing my ground here.

lines.japanese: 横断歩道の途中、この辺りでよく見かけるミニスカートの制服たちとすれ違った。
lines.english: Halfway across, I passed a cluster of the miniskirt uniforms you saw all over this neighborhood.

lines.japanese: 「あいつマジで超ヤバいって！　あと現国の山口、あいつのシャベリきもくない？　もーアレさー、ぜってー本人カッコいいと思ってんしょー」
lines.english: “That guy is, like, seriously the worst! And Yamaguchi from Japanese—doesn't the way he talks just creep you out? He totally thinks he sounds cool.”

lines.japanese: 「そそそ！　てゆか、あいつの机の上、なんか一時期アニメ的なマウスパッドあったんだってー！　でー、それ汚されたっつって！　最近なんかやたらイラついてんしー、私語したら課題追加とかゆっちゃってー」
lines.english: “Exactly! And I heard he had some anime mouse pad on his desk for a while! Then somebody ruined it, and lately he's been pissed at everything. He's all, ‘Talk in class and you get extra homework.’”

lines.japanese: 「まじで！　何ソレたるくなーい？　なんでなんで、超イミフじゃん、ありえなくなーい？」
lines.english: Seriously?! Isn't that, like, a total pain? Why, why? Makes zero sense! Is that even for real?

lines.japanese: 「あーも、やってらんね。そんでどーすん？　この後どっか寄ってく系？」
lines.english: “Ugh, I’m so done with this. So what now? We stopping somewhere after this?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、うち財布ン中、札切れだった。えー、どーしよ、鳴ちゃんは？」
lines.english: “Oh, I’m out of cash. What do we do? What about you, Naru?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、ちょお悩むかもー。わっかんなーい、いいよいいよ、みんなに合わシとく。鳴ちゃんいわゆる、右へならえ大好き民族だしィー」
lines.english: “Ooh, tough call. Dunno. Whatever you guys want is fine. I’m a proud member of the do-what-everyone-else-does tribe.”

lines.japanese: 「うっそ、鳴ちゃん欧米じゃーん。英語ペラペラ系っしょー」
lines.english: “No way, Naru, you’re practically from the West! You must be, like, totally fluent in English.”

lines.japanese: 「無理無理、ヨユーで無理。だって日本人学校ガン籠りだもん、英語なんて知らんっちゅーの」
lines.english: “Nope, nope. Not a chance. I spent the whole time holed up in a Japanese school. I don't know any English.”

lines.japanese: 「ねーねー！　そんじゃそんじゃ、白人との出会いは！　白人一杯いたんしょ！」
lines.english: “Hey, hey! Then did you meet any white people? There were tons of them, right?”

lines.japanese: 「白人？　おったおった、いっぱいおった。んとねえ、隣りのハンスさんっておいちゃんとは若干絡んだ。あ、そんでー、聞いて聞いて、そこん家の犬が超うけんの、私が行くと尻尾ガー振っちゃってー！」
lines.english: “White people? Yeah, yeah, loads. Let's see... I talked a little with Mr. Hans next door. Oh, and listen, listen—his dog was hilarious. Every time I came over, its tail went nuts!”

lines.japanese: 豪快な笑いを巻きあげながら、学生どもは跳ねるような足取りで向こう岸へと泳いでゆく。
lines.english: Whipping up a gale of laughter, the schoolgirls skipped and swam toward the opposite curb.

lines.japanese: すれ違い様の一瞬、そのうちの一人の目が俺に向けられた。ような気がする。
lines.english: For one instant as we passed, I thought one of them looked my way.

lines.japanese: でもほんの一瞬のこと。すぐに三人そろって人混みの中へ紛れて見えなくなった。
lines.english: But it was only an instant. All three soon vanished into the crowd.

lines.japanese: 俺はその姿を追いかけようと振りかえりかけて……やめる。
lines.english: I almost turned to follow them with my eyes... then stopped myself.

lines.japanese: 「青春しとけよ、小娘」
lines.english: “Enjoy your youth, kid.”

lines.japanese: 青信号が点滅する中、俺は呟きながら横断歩道を渡った。
lines.english: The green light blinked as I muttered the words and finished crossing.
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: 自動改札に切符を通そうとしたら、正面から見知った顔の女が改札をくぐってきた。さっきの三人と同じ制服。
lines.english: I was about to feed my ticket through the automatic gate when a familiar girl came through from the other side. She wore the same uniform as those three.

lines.japanese: 「あれひとり？　いよいよ鳴ちゃんにフラれた？」
lines.english: “What, all by yourself? Did Naru finally dump you?”

lines.japanese: 「うっせ」
lines.english: “Shut up.”

lines.japanese: 小娘はころころ笑いながら俺の前に立った。
lines.english: The kid stopped in front of me, laughing merrily.

lines.japanese: 「おい、そこに立たれたら俺、改札通れねえだろ。他のお客さんにも邪魔だからホレ」
lines.english: “Hey, stand there and I can't get through the gate. You're in everybody else's way too. C'mon, move.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、私？　私はいまからバイトなんだぁ」
lines.english: “Oh, me? I'm on my way to my part-time job.”

lines.japanese: 「聞いてねえよ、何いきなり話はじめてんだよ。つか、話すならこっち寄れよ」
lines.english: “Didn't ask. Why'd you suddenly start telling me your life story? And if you're gonna talk, get over here.”

lines.japanese: 俺は顎で命じて、亜衣を近くの柱まで移動させた。
lines.english: I motioned Ai over to a nearby pillar with my chin.

lines.japanese: 「なに。おまえアルバイト始めたの」
lines.english: “What, you got a part-time job?”

lines.japanese: 「えへへ、そんな誉めなくても」
lines.english: “Heh heh. You don't have to praise me that much.”

lines.japanese: 「誉めてねえよ。ガキだろうが学生だろうが、テメエの遊ぶ分ぐらい自分で稼ぐのはフツーだフツー」
lines.english: I wasn't praising you. Kid, student, whatever—you oughta earn your own spending money. That's normal. Totally normal.

lines.japanese: 「そうかもだけどー、でも亜衣ぽん超がんばってるよ？　平日週３、プラス土日祝もフルタイムで働いてんしー」
lines.english: “Maybe, but Ai-pon's working super hard, okay? Three weekdays a week, plus full-time on weekends and holidays.”

lines.japanese: 「あーそー。なに、なんか欲しいもんでもあんの」
lines.english: “Uh-huh. Saving up for something?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。次が部活のみんなと遊べる最後の春休みだし、青春して思い出作ろうぜーってことになったから、その旅行資金貯めてんの」
lines.english: “Yeah. Next spring break is our last chance for everyone in the club to hang out together, so we decided we'd take a trip and make some memories while we're young. I'm saving up for it.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、旅行。おお、いいじゃん。がんばれよ」
lines.english: “A trip, huh? Nice. Keep at it.”

lines.japanese: 「だしょー、楽しそうだしょー？　鳴ちゃんも部活が同じなら一緒に行けたんだけどねー」
lines.english: “Right? Sounds fun, doesn't it? If Naru were in the same club, she could come too.”

lines.japanese: 「二年になってからクラス違っちゃって、直接絡む機会が減ってきちゃったんだぁ。そだ、年越しはどーすんのかな。あとでメールして聞いてみよっと」
lines.english: “We got put in different classes in second year, so we don’t see each other in person as much. Oh, I wonder what she’s doing for New Year’s. I’ll email her later and ask.”

lines.japanese: 亜衣はケータイを取りだしてメールフォルダを確認していた。
lines.english: Ai took out her phone and checked her email folders.

lines.japanese: ちらりと見えた送信者の欄に、いくつか鳳鳴の名前が見えた。メールのやり取りは頻繁にしてるみたいだ。
lines.english: I glimpsed Naru Otori’s name several times in the sender column. It looked as if they emailed each other often.

lines.japanese: 「ＹＦＢのみんなはどーしよっかなー。盛り上げ役には絶好だけど、やりすぎちゃうかんなーあのひとら」
lines.english: “What should I do about the YFB guys? They're perfect for getting a party going, but they always take things too far.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、まだあいつらとツルんでんだ」
lines.english: “Oh, you still hang around with them?”

lines.japanese: 「ん、たまーにだけどね。もともとあのひとら、私の友達じゃなくてカズ君の友達だし、そのカズ君が最近疎遠になっちゃってるからさ」
lines.english: “Mm, only once in a while. They were Kazu's friends to begin with, not mine, and Kazu's been kind of distant lately.”

lines.japanese: 「森里……あんま会ってないの」
lines.english: “Morisato... You don't see him much?”

lines.japanese: 「そーなの。たまにみんなで遊ぶことはあるけど、前みたく電話かかってきたりはしないねぇ。たまにメール送っても返事そっけないし」
lines.english: “Yeah. Sometimes we all hang out, but he doesn’t call the way he used to. Even when I email him, his replies are short and cold.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん……」
俺も森里とは一年前にヘテロで別れたきりだ。きっと亜衣にも会わす顔がないんだろう。
lines.english: I hadn't seen Morisato myself since we parted at Hetero a year ago. He probably couldn't face Ai, either.

lines.japanese: 「なんかー、合コン出まくりで彼女作ってはフラれ・作ってはフラれしてるらしいよ。いいよねえ、大学生はお気楽で。ま、バニィ君情報だから、誇張入ってるかもしんないけどー」
lines.english: “Apparently he’s going on group blind dates nonstop—gets a girlfriend, gets dumped, gets another, gets dumped again. College students sure have it easy, huh? Though I heard it from Bunny, so it might be exaggerated.”

lines.japanese: 「ああそう……」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah...?”

lines.japanese: そっか、やつはやつで楽しい青春を送ってんのか。
lines.english: So he was off enjoying his youth in his own way.

lines.japanese: もしまたこの街で偶然会うことがあれば、あの必死な道化喋りを聞かせてくれるんだろうか。正直に言って、俺はちょっと再会を望んでいる。たぶん会えば会ったですぐ鬱陶しく感じるんだろうけど。
lines.english: If we happened to run into each other in this city again, would he treat me to that frantic clown act of his? Truth be told, I kind of wanted to see him again. Though the moment I did, he'd probably get on my nerves.

lines.japanese: 「つか、おまえはどうなの。彼氏とか」
lines.english: “What about you, anyway? Got a boyfriend or anything?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、気になるー？」
lines.english: “Oh? You curious?”

lines.japanese: 「全然」
lines.english: “Not remotely.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ聞くなよ！」
lines.english: “Then don't ask!”

lines.japanese: 亜衣が飛びあがって肩をぶつけてきた。そよ風のような体当たり。懐かしい。
lines.english: Ai sprang up and bumped her shoulder into mine. A body check like a passing breeze. That took me back.

lines.japanese: すこし漂った沈黙のあとに、やつはしかめた笑顔で俺を睨む。
lines.english: After a moment's silence, she glared at me through a twisted smile.

lines.japanese: 「あ、もしかして、今でも私が隼人君のこと好きとか自惚れちゃってる？　ないない、ゴメン全然ない」
lines.english: “Wait, don’t tell me you still flatter yourself that I have a thing for you. No, no. Sorry. Not at all.”

lines.japanese: 「はっ」
lines.english: “Hah.”

lines.japanese: 亜衣がぱたぱたと手を横に振る。俺は思わず苦笑いを漏らした。よかった、それなら俺も一年前に言いたかったことが言える。
lines.english: Ai fluttered one hand dismissively. A wry laugh escaped me. Good. Then I could finally say what I had wanted to tell her a year ago.

lines.japanese: 「ありがとな……今だから言うけど、あんときのおまえの好意、本当はすげー嬉しかったわ」
lines.english: “Thanks... I can say it now: the way you felt about me back then actually made me really happy.”

lines.japanese: 俺はこっ恥ずかしい気持ちになって、俯きながら後ろ頭をがしがし掻いた。
lines.english: Mortified, I dropped my gaze and raked a hand across the back of my head.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、俺行くわ。おまえもバイトがんばれよ」
lines.english: “Well, I'm off. Good luck at work.”

lines.japanese: 一方的に告げて、俺はさっさとプラットホームへ向かう。こう見えて俺はわりとシャイな男の子なんだ。
lines.english: I announced my departure and hurried toward the platform. Believe it or not, I was a fairly shy boy.

lines.japanese: 自動改札に切符を通したとき、後ろから小娘の声が聞こえたような気がした。
lines.english: As I fed my ticket through the automatic gate, I thought I heard the kid call from behind me.

lines.japanese: 「あっちゃー、真顔でそんなん正直しんどいんですけどー」
lines.english: Oof. That's honestly kinda rough when you say it with a straight face.

lines.japanese: だけど内容は雑踏に紛れてよく聞こえなかった。
lines.english: But her words dissolved into the crowd, and I couldn't make them out.

lines.japanese: 「てか気付けよなー、いまだに未練ばりばり１００％だってのー。もー、鳴ちゃんに会うのが辛いのだって、どー考えたっておまえのせいだろがよー」
lines.english: “Seriously, take a hint already. I'm still one hundred percent hung up on you. And why do you think seeing Naru hurts so much? Obviously that's your fault too.”

lines.japanese: 「ばかやろー、はやくフラれちゃえ……」
lines.english: “Idiot. Hurry up and get dumped...”

lines.japanese: 「いつまで待てばいいんだよ……」
lines.english: “How long am I supposed to wait...?”

lines.japanese: 駅から降りてコンビニに寄りつつ、ぶらぶらと帰路についた。
lines.english: I got off the train, stopped at a convenience store, and wandered home.

lines.japanese: この風景もだいぶ見慣れてきた。たぶん俺には似合ってないだろうが、そんな中を当たり前のように歩くのも悪くない。
lines.english: The view had become thoroughly familiar. It probably didn't suit me, but walking through it as if I belonged wasn't half bad.

lines.japanese: 俺はポリ袋ひとつ提げてあいつの家へ向かった。
lines.english: A single plastic bag dangling from one hand, I headed for her place.

lines.japanese: 「うーす、邪魔しまーす」
lines.english: “Hey. Coming in.”

lines.japanese: 最近のマンションってのは、玄関を開けると勝手に電気がつくものらしい。便利。超便利。
lines.english: Apparently, in modern apartment buildings, the entryway light came on by itself when you opened the door. Handy. Super handy.

lines.japanese: 俺はもらい物の安全靴を適当に脱ぎちらかすと、ぺたんぺたん廊下を歩いて、リビングの椅子に腰をおろした。
lines.english: I kicked off the safety boots someone had given me, padded down the hall, and dropped into a chair in the living room.

lines.japanese: 「……つっても、まあ、まだ帰ってねえか」
lines.english: “...Though I guess she's not home yet.”

lines.japanese: 現場の都合で、今日は仕事が休みだ。そんな日は、俺の方が先に帰ってくることもままある。
lines.english: I had the day off because there was no work for me at the site. On days like this, I often got home before she did.

lines.japanese: 鳴のとーちゃんが年単位で単身赴任中なのをいいことに、俺はこうしてしょっちゅう鳳邸へ遊びに来ていた。そのまま泊まったりすることもある──
lines.english: Taking full advantage of Naru's dad being away on a years-long posting, I had become a frequent visitor to the Otori residence. Sometimes I even stayed the night—

lines.japanese: ──まあ、うざい兄貴や家政婦のおばちゃんがいる日は、さすがに遠慮するけどな。
lines.english: —though I still stayed away if her annoying brother or the housekeeper was around.

lines.japanese: 貧乏性の俺には、ぶっちゃけ羽田の家ぐらい庶民的な内装の方がなにかと居心地いい。
lines.english: I was too used to living cheap; a place furnished like the Haneda house was honestly more my speed.

lines.japanese: でも、いつだったか鳴がか細い声で、俺がここにいるとこの家もそんなに広く感じられないと言った。その頃から俺は、できるかぎりここへ「帰る」ようになった。
lines.english: But once, in a tiny voice, Naru had said the house did not feel quite so large when I was there. After that, I began coming *home* here whenever I could.

lines.japanese: よし、じゃあ鳴もいないことだし、今のうちにアレをやっつけとこう。
lines.english: All right. Naru wasn't around, so I might as well get *that* taken care of now.

lines.japanese: 俺は鳴の机を借りるために、リビングからやつの部屋へ移動した。
lines.english: I left the living room for Naru's bedroom to borrow her desk.

lines.japanese: 「おそーい！」
lines.english: “You're laaate!”

lines.japanese: 「あれ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 開けた瞬間怒られた。
lines.english: She let me have it the instant I opened the door.

lines.japanese: 部屋着の鳴が、センザンコウの置物を抱いたままベッドから跳ねおきてきた。
lines.english: Naru, in her lounging clothes and clutching her pangolin figurine, sprang up from the bed.

lines.japanese: 「あ、先帰ってたんだ……」
lines.english: “Oh. You beat me home...”

lines.japanese: てっきり学校の連中と遊びまわって、夜まで帰ってこないと思ってた。
lines.english: I'd assumed she would be out with her school friends until nighttime.

lines.japanese: 俺はただいまと言いながらクッションにケツを落とした。あからさまに鳴がぷんすかしているので、若干肩身が狭い。
lines.english: I said, ‘I'm home,’ and dropped onto a cushion. Naru was visibly huffing and puffing, which made me feel a little sheepish.

lines.japanese: 「遅いですよー、せっかく私、友達とベーグル諦めて帰ってきたのにー」
lines.english: “You're late. I gave up bagels with my friends and came straight home for you.”

lines.japanese: 俺の正面に、鳴ともの言わぬ友人が座った。
lines.english: Naru and her silent friend settled opposite me.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そう……悪りい……」
lines.english: “Oh... Sorry...”

lines.japanese: 目を逸らしながら言ったら、ぬっと友人を突きつけられた。つぶらな黒目が俺を見つめている。
lines.english: I said it with my eyes averted, and she thrust her friend into my face. Two round black eyes stared into mine.

lines.japanese: 「さあセンザンコウさんにも謝りなさい」
lines.english: “Now apologize to Mr. Pangolin too.”

lines.japanese: 「ごめんなさい」
lines.english: “I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 俺はセンザンコウさんに頭を下げた。
lines.english: I bowed my head to Mr. Pangolin.

lines.japanese: 「さっき交差点ですれ違ったじゃないですかー。はー、もー、あの時声かけてくれればよかったのにー」
lines.english: “We passed each other at the intersection earlier! Honestly, you could've called out to me then.”

lines.japanese: 鳴は文句を言いながら、ずりずりとクッションごと前進してくる。近い近い。俺は顔をしかめたが無駄だった。
lines.english: Still complaining, Naru scraped forward, cushion and all. Too close. I grimaced, to no effect.

lines.japanese: 「んーな……べつに声かけたってしょーがねえだろ。俺、おまえの友達と話すことなんかねえし」
lines.english: Wh—what'd be the point? I've got nothing to talk about with your friends.

lines.japanese: 「やー、学校では私、強くて優しくて頼り甲斐のある男性と付きあってることになっててー、紹介してくれって前からせっつかれてるんですよー」
lines.english: “At school, I'm apparently dating a strong, kind, dependable man, and they've been pestering me for ages to introduce him.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょ、待ておまえ、なにそんな本当のこと勝手に広めてンだよ。いくら俺がまったくその通りのナイスガイだからって、事前にハードル上げられたら流石にプレッシャーかかんだろ」
lines.english: “Wait. Why're you spreading such accurate information without permission? Sure, I'm exactly that kind of great guy, but when you set the bar that high in advance, even I feel the pressure.”

lines.japanese: 「あーいえ、私はそんなこと一言も言っていないんですが、勝手にクラスの皆さんが尾ひれを一枚二枚三枚と付けたしてしまってー」
lines.english: “Oh, no. I never said a word of that. Everyone in class just kept adding to the story. A detail here, another there, a third for luck.”

lines.japanese: 「ぜんぶ尾ひれかよ。いや、おまえも一言ぐらいは言っとけよ。ニヒルかクールかハードボイルドの、どれか一つぐらいは言っとけよ」
lines.english: “So they made it all up? You could’ve put in one good word yourself. Brooding, cool, hard-boiled—any one of those would’ve done.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ブラックホールとは言っておきましたー」
lines.english: “Oh, I did tell them 'black hole.'”

lines.japanese: 「そこまでハードル下げなくていいんだよ。つかおまえのクラスの連中、なんでそんな設定から、強くて優しくて頼り甲斐のある男が想像できんだよ」
lines.english: “You didn't have to lower the bar *that* far. And how did your classmates get from that description to a strong, kind, dependable man?”

lines.japanese: 「だから今日はいい機会だと思ったのに、もー、なんで私あんなワケあり不倫カップルみたいに、擦れちがった彼氏を無視しなきゃいけないんですかー」
lines.english: “That’s why I thought today was the perfect chance. Why did I have to ignore my own boyfriend in the street like we were having some messy affair?”

lines.japanese: 俺のあぐらに手を置いて鳴が迫る。
lines.english: Naru planted her hands on my crossed legs and leaned in.

lines.japanese: 「っせえなあ、だからそーゆーの苦手なんだよ」
lines.english: “God, you're annoying. I told you, I'm no good at that stuff.”

lines.japanese: 俺は背を反らせて距離を離した。
lines.english: I leaned back to put some distance between us.

lines.japanese: この話題はこれまで何度も持ちあがっているが、鳴はなかなか引きさがってくれない。しょせん女子供には、硬派を目指す男心が理解できないみたいだ。
lines.english: This had come up plenty of times before, but Naru refused to let it go. Women and kids simply couldn’t understand a guy trying to be old-school tough.

lines.japanese: こういうときは話を変えるしかない。
lines.english: At times like this, my only option was to change the subject.

lines.japanese: 「おまえこそ、なんで奴らと俺とで、喋り方違うんだよ」
lines.english: “What about you? Why do you talk one way with them and another way with me?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、花も恥じらう乙女たちの会話をちゃっかり盗み聞きですか。そういうのはいくら彼氏でもよくないですよ」
lines.english: “My, were you shamelessly eavesdropping on a conversation among maidens fair enough to shame the flowers? Even a boyfriend shouldn't do that.”

lines.japanese: 「馬鹿、あんなでかい声で話してたら誰だって聞こえるっつの。てかおまえ、完全に馴染んでたじゃねえか」
lines.english: “Idiot. At that volume, anybody could hear you. Besides, you fit right in.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、えー、郷に入りてはというか、朱に交わればというか、多少無理してる部分はあるんですがだいぶ自然にスイッチ切りかわるようにはなってきましたー」
lines.english: Umm, well, when in Rome, do as the Romans do. Or maybe, you become the company you keep. Part of it's still a little forced, but the switch comes pretty naturally now.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そ」
lines.english: “Oh. That so.”

lines.japanese: 「やー、でもやっぱり隼人さん相手がいちばん楽に話せますよねー」
lines.english: “Still, talking to you is easiest of all, Hayato.”

lines.japanese: 鳴はアホみたいに口を開けて目を細めた。
lines.english: Naru let her mouth hang open like an idiot and narrowed her eyes.

lines.japanese: ま、たしかに俺も、こいつといる時が一番楽だ。感謝のツッコミをデコに一発くれてやろう。
lines.english: Well, she was right. I was most at ease with her too. A little bop on the forehead ought to show my appreciation.

lines.japanese: 「口閉じろ口」
lines.english: “Close your mouth.”

lines.japanese: 「たはー」
lines.english: “Heh.”

lines.japanese: なんてノロケてる場合じゃない。どうせ今日は泊まりになる、そういうのはあとでたっぷりやろう。
lines.english: But this was no time to sit here getting lovey-dovey. I was staying the night anyway, so we could do plenty of that later.

lines.japanese: 「机借りんぞ」
lines.english: “I'm borrowing your desk.”

lines.japanese: 俺はコンビニ袋を掴んで立ちあがった。
lines.english: I grabbed the convenience-store bag and stood.

lines.japanese: 「はー、なんですかそれー？」
lines.english: “Huh? What's that?”

lines.japanese: 「履歴書。現場の監督に持ってこいって言われた」
lines.english: “My résumé. The foreman told me to bring one in.”

lines.japanese: 「あー！　もしかして就職ですか、うはー、おめでとうございますー！」
lines.english: “Oh! Is it for a permanent job? Wow, congratulations!”

lines.japanese: 「まだ分かんねえって。持ってくだけ持ってくだけ」
lines.english: “Don't know yet. I'm just bringing it in, that's all.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、理想のタイプは家庭のために働くひとですー」
lines.english: Mmm. My ideal guy works hard for his family.

lines.japanese: 「聞いてねえよ」
lines.english: “Didn't ask.”

lines.japanese: 「そして作業着ー」
lines.english: “And wears work clothes.”

lines.japanese: 「口閉じろ口」
lines.english: “Close your mouth.”
